per_question.question: Under what conditions can speech therapy be provided via telehealth under NC Medicaid?
per_question.agent_answer:
Speech therapy may be provided by telehealth under NC Medicaid when it is **medically necessary, clinically appropriate for telehealth, and delivered under the general telehealth rules in Policy 1-H**.

## Conditions NC Medicaid requires

### 1. The speech therapy itself must be medically necessary
Clinical Coverage Policy 10A covers speech-language therapy only when the beneficiary meets the policy’s medical-necessity standards. For example, speech-language therapy for dysphagia must have documented findings supporting one of the listed deficits, and the evaluation must include specified clinical findings. [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) § 3.2.1.3.  
Speech-language-audiology therapy is also limited to the number of **medically necessary** visits within an authorization period, which cannot exceed **six calendar months**. [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) § 5.4.2.

### 2. The service must be safe and effective to deliver by telehealth
NC Medicaid’s telehealth policy requires providers to ensure the service **can be safely and effectively delivered** using telehealth. The provider must consider:
- the beneficiary’s **behavioral, physical, and cognitive abilities** to participate,
- the beneficiary’s **safety** given the complexity of the service, and
- if a caregiver or facilitator is needed, that person’s **ability and safety** as well.  
[Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) § 3.2.1.

### 3. Telehealth delivery must meet professional and privacy standards
The provider must ensure telehealth delivery conforms to:
- professional standards of care,
- ethical practice,
- scope-of-practice requirements, and
- other relevant federal, state, and institutional requirements.  
The provider must also protect beneficiary privacy and confidentiality to the best of their ability. [Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) § 3.2.1.

### 4. Consent and identity verification are required
Before telehealth services are delivered, the provider must:
- obtain and document **verbal or written consent** (or document why consent could not be obtained in extenuating circumstances), and
- verify the beneficiary’s identity using **two points of identification**.  
[Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) § 3.2.1.

### 5. The beneficiary must still be allowed in-person care
A beneficiary **cannot be forced to use telehealth**. NC Medicaid says beneficiaries are not required to seek services through telehealth and must be allowed access to **in-person services if requested**. [Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) § 3.2.1.

### 6. Telehealth cannot be mainly for convenience
Telehealth services must be individualized and not furnished in a manner primarily intended for the convenience of the beneficiary, caregiver, or provider. [Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) § 3.1.

## Bottom line
NC Medicaid allows speech therapy by telehealth **when the underlying speech therapy is otherwise covered and medically necessary, and when the provider determines telehealth is a safe, effective, clinically appropriate way to deliver that service for that beneficiary**. The provider must also meet Policy 1-H requirements on consent, identity verification, privacy, professional standards, and access to in-person care. [Clinical Coverage Policy 10A](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/10a-outpatient-specialized-therapies/download?attachment) §§ 3.2.1.3, 5.4.2; [Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/1h-telehealth-virtual-communications-and-remote-patient-monitoring/download?attachment) §§ 3.1, 3.2.1.

## Federal point
I could not verify from the retrieved text of [42 CFR Part 410](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-410) that it adds a speech-therapy-specific telehealth condition beyond the NC Medicaid policy requirements above. The federal section retrieved was about diagnostic tests, not speech therapy telehealth conditions.

**Current documents checked for amendments:** Clinical Coverage Policy 10A (effective 2/1/2025), Clinical Coverage Policy 1-H (effective 2/1/2025), and 42 CFR Part 410; no later amendments were returned by the amendment records for those documents.
